title: Stochastic linear bandits on a Euclidean ball with independent scalar Gaussian noise.
summary: The learner chooses actions in the Euclidean unit ball and observes their inner products with a fixed unknown parameter plus independent standard Gaussian noise. The target is cumulative mean reward relative to the best fixed action. Reducing action magnitude does not reduce the noise variance.

task.formulation_latex: Y_t=\langle x_t,\theta\rangle+Z_t,\quad Z_t\overset{\mathrm{i.i.d.}}\sim\mathcal N(0,1),\qquad R_T=\sum_t(\|\theta\|_2-\langle x_t,\theta\rangle)
description_paragraphs: The learner chooses actions in the Euclidean unit ball and observes their inner products with a fixed unknown parameter plus independent standard Gaussian noise. The target is cumulative mean reward relative to the best fixed action. Reducing action magnitude does not reduce the noise variance.

model.instance: Actions satisfy $x_t\in B_2^d(1)$ and the unknown parameter satisfies $\theta\in B_2^d(1)$. Observe $Y_t=\langle x_t,\theta\rangle+Z_t$, with independent standard Gaussian $Z_t$. Noise is added after the inner product, and its variance does not scale with action length.

assumptions.description: Noise is added outside the inner product. Conditional on any action $x$, it is $\mathcal N(0,1)$, with variance independent of $\|x\|_2$.

model.parameter_domain_description: T: $T\in\mathbb N,\ T\ge1$ (public); d: $d\in\mathbb N,\ d\ge1$ (public)
interaction_timing: The parameter $\theta$ is fixed; $d,T$, the action domain, and noise variance are public.
The learner selects x_t from the history.
Accumulate the mean gap ||theta||_2-<x_t,theta> and continue to the next round.
model.adversary_information: The unknown distribution or parameter is fixed before interaction. Learner randomness and sample randomness are independent. No adversary changes the distribution round by round from the learner's history.
unresolved_applicability: General sub-Gaussian noise, parameter-vector noise, and other action geometries each require separate checks of the native oracle and parameter window.
description_paragraphs: The hidden reward parameter $\theta$ is fixed before interaction and satisfies $\|\theta\|_2\le1$.
Scalar observation noise is i.i.d. $Z_t\sim N(0,1)$ and independent of the pre-action history. The observation variance remains one even when $x_t=0$. This specification uses additive scalar noise.
The actual action is also the sole observation point and satisfies $\|x_t\|_2\le1$.
Require $d,T\ge1$. Both actions and the unknown parameter lie in the unit Euclidean ball.

operations.query_signature: Input: $t,\ x_t\in B_2^d(1)$. The specification's protocol governs timing and visible information.

feedback_quality.description: Choose x_t, then draw Z_t and return one scalar. Neither theta, a gradient, nor another directional projection in the same round is revealed. Repeating x in another round uses fresh noise and is charged again.

operations.coupling: Choose x_t, then draw Z_t and return one scalar. Neither theta, a gradient, nor another directional projection in the same round is revealed. Repeating x in another round uses fresh noise and is charged again.
operations.index_control: The learner selects feasible actions and any probes permitted by the specification. The environment determines current losses, outcomes, or fresh samples. The learner cannot select future rounds.
operations.access_schedule: Interaction follows the sequence in registry.protocols. Current loss feedback is available only after the action is submitted. Any pre-action disclosure of context or advice is specified separately.

auxiliary_interfaces: No additional access to hidden losses, means, or gradients is available. Projection, sampling, and internal optimization over public domains may have separately recorded computation costs; they are not free loss oracles.
description_paragraphs: Linear rewards with independent scalar noise:

$$
t,\ x_t\in B_2^d(1)\ \longmapsto\ Y_t\mid\mathcal{H}_{t-1},x_t\sim\mathcal{N}(\langle x_t,\theta\rangle,1)
$$
Choose action $x_t$, then draw fresh noise $Z_t$ and return one scalar observation.
Neither $\theta$, a gradient, nor projections onto other directions in the same round are returned.
The same x may be measured again in another round, with fresh noise and a new charge.
Public inputs are $d,T$, action domain $B_2^d(1)$, parameter-norm bound one, and known scalar noise $\mathcal N(0,1)$.

output.feasibility: Every loss-bearing action must belong to the action domain. The final output retains the complete action trajectory.
output.allowed_postprocessing: Any measurable computation on received feedback is allowed. No native observation may be added after the budget is exhausted or the algorithm stops.
output.certificate_requirement: Only the stated statistical guarantee is required, not a certificate verifiable through the feedback interface.
description_paragraphs: The output is the complete action trajectory satisfying feasibility and timing requirements. Randomized mixtures may be implemented before acting. Retrospective averages or convex combinations cannot replace actions that have already incurred loss. No additional optimal value or certificate is required.

metric.normalization: Use the cumulative quantity over T rounds without dividing by T. Preserve the displayed order of probability or expectation.
metric.finiteness_conditions: The unit mean/loss range or the stated Lipschitz amplitude bound limits the per-round excess loss to two. Cumulative regret is therefore at most 2T. Unbounded observation noise does not enter pseudo-regret.

bounds.derivation: The source lower bound writes ambient dimension as $d+2$. If actual dimension is denoted $D$, then $D\ge3$ implies $D-2\ge D/3$, so relabeling preserves the order. For $D=1,2$, embed the two parameters $\theta=\pm ae_1$ with $a=1/(4\sqrt T)$. Under any policy the KL divergence between transcript laws is at most $2a^2T=1/8$. Pinsker's inequality gives constant sign-error probability and cumulative regret $\Omega(\sqrt T)$. Since $\min\{T,D\sqrt T\}\le2\sqrt T$, the required order also holds in these small dimensions.
